name: Ecopetrol S.A.

profile.description: Ecopetrol S.A. is Colombia's majority state-owned integrated oil and gas company, founded in 1948, operating Exploration & Production, Transportation & Logistics (pipelines) and Refining & Petrochemicals segments; its ADRs trade on the NYSE [7]. With Brent averaging ~$97/bbl, Q2 2026 revenue rose 35.5% YoY to COP 40.2T, EBITDA reached COP 17.7T (44% margin) and net income attributable to owners more than tripled to COP 6.1T [1]. Leadership has been unstable: President Ricardo Roa took leave in April 2026, acting president Juan Carlos Hurtado retired on September 15, 2026, and CFO Alfonso Camilo Barco is now acting CEO [3]. Q3 2026 results are due November 10, 2026 [2]. Market cap ~$35B.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): No transformative product or business-model shift was evident in 2026 disclosures; recent initiatives are incremental, such as a new sulfur-solidification plant at the Cartagena refinery announced by the acting president [4]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI-driven savings were found in company or press materials. Market Share (1/2): As Colombia's national integrated producer spanning upstream, pipelines and refining, Ecopetrol is the meaningful domestic incumbent, but it is a price-taker in global crude with no share-gain evidence [7]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management says it has a defined strategic plan and is reviewing assets in and outside Colombia, and has reopened technical discussion of fracking, but no dated project pipeline with revenue visibility was disclosed [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D expense is reported in the income statement [7].
innovation.label: WEAK

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Ecopetrol's public positioning centers on energy production and 'value creation and sustainability' — generic for a national oil company and frequently subordinated to government policy [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No specific community-investment programs with dollar amounts were identified; instead, the 2025 EIA/Earthworks 'Crude Lies' investigation, based on leaked internal 'Iguana Papers', alleges more than 600 cases of major soil and water contamination in 2010–2016 with about a fifth concealed from authorities [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): Three different leaders have run the company in 2026 alone (Roa on leave, Hurtado acting then retiring, Barco acting), and no retention data was found [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider purchases found; majority state ownership limits the relevance of this signal [7].
inspiration.label: WEAK

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend-sleeve stock (yield 3.78%, dividends paid since 2008): 9.10/10, rounded to 9. D/E of 95.7% scores 0.89; ROE of 15.95% scores 1.0; revenue growth of 35.5% (latest quarter YoY) scores 1.0; the FY2020–FY2025 5-year revenue CAGR of 17.3% (derived from FMP statements; FY2020 was a COVID trough, flattering the figure) scores 1.0; forward P/E of 8.53 scores 1.0; profit margin of 10.2% scores 0.51 [1][7]. Payout ratio of 52.5% scores 0.79, and 19 consecutive years of payments scores 1.0 at 2x weight [6][7]. Consecutive years of dividend growth and 5-year dividend CAGR are excluded (null) because Ecopetrol's variable, earnings-linked dividend has been cut and raised across cycles and no reliable verified series was available. Liquidity passes easily at ~$28M of average daily dollar volume.
infrastructure.label: STRONG

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): IMMUNE. Ecopetrol extracts, transports and refines physical hydrocarbons; AI cannot substitute for crude oil, pipelines or refineries, and no analyst commentary identifies AI substitution risk. Its earnings are driven by Brent prices (~$97/bbl in Q2 2026), production volumes and Colombian fiscal policy rather than technology disruption [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue is disclosed.
ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK

infinite_game.summary: Ecopetrol plays a finite game set by Colombia's political cycle. Its purpose shifts with each government — with the fracking debate intensifying under Roa and the interim leadership now reopening technical discussion of it — and leadership has turned over three times in 2026, with an S&P downgrade to BB- along the way [3][4]. A 78-year national-champion role gives it endurance, but not a self-directed Just Cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The company's stated purpose of supplying Colombia's energy while creating value and advancing sustainability reads as a policy mandate rather than a Just Cause; it changes emphasis with each administration and does not visibly drive strategy [4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Leadership instability — Roa's April 2026 leave, Hurtado's appointment as acting president in July and retirement on September 15, and Barco's interim appointment — plus whistleblower allegations of concealed environmental damage point to a politicized, low-trust environment [3][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): As a state-backed domestic incumbent, Ecopetrol shows no evidence of framing competitors as worthy rivals; competitive language centers on national production and reserves.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has adjusted strategy — reviewing assets inside and outside Colombia, adding refinery environmental capacity, and reopening the fracking debate — but these are incremental and politically driven rather than a cause-driven reinvention [4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Interim leaders have emphasized near-term operating priorities and possibly raising targets, while governance has been shaped by government intervention; there is no record of leadership sacrificing near-term results for a long-term cause [3][4].

investment_thesis: Ecopetrol is a cash machine when oil is high: Q2 2026 revenue rose 35.5% to COP 40.2T, EBITDA hit COP 17.7T at a 44% margin and net income attributable to owners jumped to COP 6.1T from COP 1.8T a year earlier, with Brent averaging ~$97/bbl [1]. The ADR trades at 8.5x forward earnings and ~4.5x EV/EBITDA, yields ~3.8% with a ~52% payout, and generates ROE near 16% [7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is political and commodity risk. FY2025 revenue fell 16% to COP 111.5T and net income to COP 8.4T as oil weakened, showing how quickly earnings reverse; S&P cut the company to BB-, and D/E of ~96% (123% on FMP's measure) limits flexibility [3][7]. Governance is fragile — three leaders in 2026 — and the 'Iguana Papers' allegations of concealed contamination expose the company to regulatory and SEC scrutiny [3][5]. The stock has already nearly doubled from its $9.10 52-week low [7].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results on November 10, 2026, which should again reflect elevated Brent (~$97/bbl in Q2) and a large YoY earnings increase [1][2]
Appointment of a permanent CEO after the 2026 presidential selection process, potentially stabilizing governance [3]
Reopened technical discussion of unconventional (fracking) development and asset reviews that could expand reserves life [4]
key_risks: Oil-price reversal: FY2025 showed revenue falling 16% and net income to COP 8.4T when crude weakened; Q2 2026 gains are price-driven [1][7]
Governance and political interference — three leaders in 2026, majority state ownership and an S&P downgrade to BB- [3]
Environmental and legal exposure from the EIA/Earthworks 'Crude Lies' report alleging concealed contamination and a whistleblower request for SEC investigation [5]
